reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `http-retries` (`b04b610`) against `main` (`5f9be03`). Three findings:

1. *High — `timeoutMs: 0` no longer disables timeouts* — `src/http.js:11`  
   `opts.timeoutMs || DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` converts `0` into 10,000. The nightly export explicitly passes `0` (`src/export.js:4`), so exports taking over 10 seconds to receive headers will now abort. Confirmed: main schedules no timer; this branch schedules 10,000 ms. Restore the nullish default (`??`) and add a zero-timeout regression test.

2. *High — retries replay non-idempotent requests by default* — `src/http.js:30–33`  
   Retry eligibility considers only response status, not HTTP method or replay safety. A POST that performs a side effect but returns 503 can now execute three times without the caller opting in. An in-memory probe confirmed one POST on main versus three here. Restrict automatic retries to safe/idempotent operations, with explicit opt-in for other requests and replayable bodies.

3. *Medium — discarded retry responses aren’t drained or cancelled* — `src/http.js:31–33`  
   Intermediate 429/5xx responses are abandoned before the next fetch. With streaming responses, that can retain connections and exhaust a constrained pool during an outage—the exact time retries are busiest. A probe confirmed two discarded bodies and zero cancellations. Consume or cancel each discarded body before retrying; leave the final response available to the caller.

*Validation:* all three existing tests pass, but none covers these cases. Ran additional read-only, in-memory probes; no files were changed.
